open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure identity
open_points.text: The migration closure (M10), kept as a record of its own by the owner's decision of 2026-10-31, is an entity identified by the digest of the file it accepted: a value cannot be a record of its own (SPEC_STANDARD §15.1.1).
open_points.question: Was the owner's 2026-10-31 acceptance of M10 an acceptance of the then-written value model, as the Status says, or a decision that it is an entity as this passage says?
options: M10 remains the value accepted as written on 2026-10-31
M10 is an entity under a separate owner decision that supersedes the accepted value model
open_points.default_guess: Treat the 2026-11-11 entity declaration as a new decision superseding the former value model.

open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure identity scope
open_points.text: It is identified by the digest of the file the import accepted, the one identity it has (codex round-04 T1); Registry mints no identifier for it.
open_points.question: If separate store histories successfully accept files with the same digest, do their MigrationClosure records have the same entity identity or distinct identities scoped by store history?
options: The digest is globally sufficient, so both records have the same identity
Identity is the pair of store-history identity and file digest
Each successful import event has a distinct identity not fully expressed by the digest
open_points.default_guess: Scope the digest by store history so each history owns a distinct closure.

witness.initial: Production is restored from a backup made before its first successful import.
events: The owner imports file F successfully, creating a closure identified by F's digest.
After a loss, the owner restores the pre-import backup outside Registry.
The owner imports the same file F successfully again.
outcomes: Both closures are the same entity because their sole identity is the same digest.
The two store histories own distinct closure entities even though the digest is equal.
witness.observer: A maintainer implementing persistence, references, or audit linkage across restored histories

open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure publisher reference
open_points.text: it is the record a pointer the import brought in names as its publisher (M05)
open_points.question: Does an imported artifact pointer name the MigrationClosure record as its publisher, or does it name the owner or agent who published it as R0-88 requires?
options: The imported pointer names MigrationClosure as publisher
The imported pointer names an acting principal; MigrationClosure may be linked separately
Import rewrites the pointer's publisher to the owner performing the import
open_points.default_guess: Keep the acting principal as publisher and represent any import provenance separately.

witness.initial: The VPS export contains an artifact pointer selected for import.
events: The owner confirms and completes the import.
A caller later reads the pointer's artifact history.
outcomes: The pointer's publisher is the MigrationClosure record.
The pointer's publisher is the owner or agent who published it, as required by R0-88.
witness.observer: The owner reading artifact provenance or the audit history

open_points.subject: M12 AuditSequence creation lifecycle
open_points.text: Registry makes it, with number 0, in the transaction that makes a new, empty store (State 2 A17 rule 5) and never makes a second one.
open_points.question: How does a non-empty store that already exists when M12 is introduced acquire its required AuditSequence record, and what value and identity does that record receive?
options: A schema migration creates it from the greatest sequence ever used
Startup creates it when absent from information still present in the store
Existing stores are unsupported and must be rebuilt as new empty stores
The model is deemed to have existed historically, with no explicit creation transition
open_points.default_guess: Create it in a one-time store migration using the durable last-ever sequence value, failing closed if that value cannot be established.

witness.initial: A production store already contains audit entries when software containing the newly added M12 model is deployed.
events: The next significant change needs to append an audit entry.
outcomes: Registry first creates AuditSequence from the store's prior audit history and allocates the next unused number.
Registry assumes AuditSequence exists only for newly created stores and cannot append correctly, or starts it at 0 and reuses numbers.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log and any verifier relying on sequence uniqueness

open_points.subject: Status and model field declarations
open_points.text: Field names, types, formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0, "Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).
open_points.question: Replace the deferral of model field names and types with complete typed field declarations for every State 1 model; only answer shapes and other matters outside model structure may remain deferred.
